correctness.rationale: The multiplication is \( (a,b)(c,d)=(0,ac+ad+bd)\). Product terms therefore have zero \(e\)-coordinate. Their \(f\)-coordinates form an ideal in the full Boolean function algebra because left and right multiplication by a variable recover multiplication by both coordinate functions. The diagonal product \(q_{ii}=a_i+a_ib_i+b_i\) is the indicator of a nonzero coordinate, so these generators have only the all-zero common zero and generate exactly all functions vanishing there, of dimension \(4^n-1\). The variable span contributes a disjoint \(n\)-dimensional subspace. This proves \(\dim F_n=4^n+n-1\) for every \(n\ge1\). The bundled checker independently reproduces dimensions \(4,17,66\) for \(n=1,2,3\); the finite computation is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating paper establishes only the maximal exponential scale for this concrete nonsimple prime example. The exact formula gives a sharp model of that phenomenon at every finite rank and identifies the mechanism: products generate the entire codimension-one Boolean-function ideal. This is a structural strengthening rather than a numerical recomputation, and it can serve as a benchmark for exact-growth questions for other small prime nonassociative rings.
